events.name: The Spearow Storm
events.intro: A Spearow on a branch. A stone on the path. Your lead looks at the stone, and at you, as if to say: don't. The battle before this one went badly, or went long. Somebody's thrown something, you or a child or nobody. It doesn't matter. The Spearow's seen who's standing nearest. It calls. The tree behind it empties into the air. Rain. Your most tired Pokémon is down in the mud, and when the Ball's held out, it turns its head away.

success.text: The flock dives. You don't move. The Pokémon behind you gets up, and it fights like nothing has ever been asked of it before.
You run, and the mud tries to keep your shoes. Behind you the flock wheels once, and loses interest. Nothing lost.

failure.text: Caught at the treeline. Three Spearow, and nowhere left to run.

success.text: It looks at you for a long moment. It goes in. Then you run, and the flock lets you.

events.name: The Spearow Storm: After
events.intro: The rain stops as if it's been switched off. Something crosses the sky from one edge to the other. It's gold, and it's very large, and it leaves a colour behind it that you haven't got a word for. One feather comes down. It's gone before it lands.

success.text: The flock has scattered. Nothing is given now but the Bond, and the colour, which you'll keep.

effects.text: Stood in front of a Spearow flock in the rain, and saw something gold cross the sky.

events.name: The Pokémon Center Siege
events.intro: The party's in the machine. The nurse is counting under her breath. The lights go out. Glass, from above. A rope. Two shapes and a smaller one, landing in a pose in the dark, where nobody can see it. Jessie: "Prepare for—" James: "They can't see us, Jess." Meowth: "Do it anyway. It's the principle." The nurse, low, pushing a tray at you: "Yours are mid-cycle. I can't pull them. These are from storage. People leave them. I don't know what's in them. Go."

choices.label: Take a Ball from the tray.

success.text: Three rental Poké Balls. One is always empty.

failure.text: You throw it. It opens. Nothing. Meowth: "...Was that it? Was that the attack?" It costs the turn, and nothing else.

events.name: The Siege: In the Dark
events.intro: In the dark, nobody can aim. Ekans and Koffing first, then Meowth himself.

success.text: Accuracy is a guess for both sides. The rentals fight like they've been waiting a long time to be asked.

events.name: The Siege: The Machine Chimes
events.intro: The machine chimes. Your own lead's out of it, half-healed, and it's furious on the nurse's behalf.

choices.label: Send in your lead, at half HP.

success.text: It knows whose Center this is.
The rentals again. One of them has decided it likes you.

events.name: The Siege: The Ending
events.intro: The lights come back one bank at a time. Three people, caught halfway up a rope.

success.text: They climb. James needs a leg up; you give it. The Center heals easier for the rest of Kanto. One of the rentals fought well; the nurse says its owner never came back, and it may be kept.

effects.text: Held the Viridian Pokémon Center in the dark with three borrowed Poké Balls.

success.text: You hold them for the police. Officer Jenny comes. They've gone by then; they always have. The Center heals easier for the rest of Kanto.

effects.text: Held the Viridian Pokémon Center in the dark with three borrowed Poké Balls.

success.text: James: "...We could chip in." He means it. Jessie pays. It's four coins and a button. The Center heals easier for the rest of Kanto.

effects.text: Held the Viridian Pokémon Center in the dark with three borrowed Poké Balls.

events.name: The Siege: Gone
events.intro: The trio take one common thing from the counter and leave. The Pokémon in the machine aren't touched.

choices.label: Let the nurse turn the lights on.

success.text: Nothing of yours was taken. The nurse sweeps the glass, and doesn't say anything, and gives you a Poké Ball anyway.

events.name: The Healer in the Straw Hat
events.intro: The forest's edge. A child in a straw hat too big for them, with a fishing rod they aren't using, watching your worst-off Pokémon. "That one's tired in a way sleeping won't fix. Can I hold it? I'll give it back." They don't wait long for an answer. They don't reach, either. They hold their arms out and leave it to the Pokémon.

success.text: The child closes their eyes. The forest goes quiet the way a room does. When they open them, the Pokémon's standing, and the child's swaying. "There. It was mostly worried about you." They're asleep on their feet before you've said thank you. A Pikachu with a flower behind its ear leads them off by the sleeve.

effects.text: Let a child in a straw hat listen to where it hurt.

success.text: The child closes their eyes. The forest goes quiet the way a room does. When they open them, the Pokémon's standing, and the child's swaying. "There. It was mostly worried about you." And to the Shadow Pokémon: "Oh. Somebody shut a door in you. I can't open it. I can oil the hinge." They're asleep on their feet before you've said thank you. A Pikachu with a flower behind its ear leads them off by the sleeve.

effects.text: Let a child in a straw hat listen to where it hurt.

success.text: "I don't know what it's called. I ask it where it hurts. Then I listen. It's the listening that does it."
They nod, as if that was an answer too, and go back to not fishing. Coins left on the stump would still be there at the end of the region.

events.name: The Healer in the Straw Hat
events.intro: They're still holding their arms out.

success.text: The child closes their eyes. The forest goes quiet the way a room does. When they open them, the Pokémon's standing, and the child's swaying. "There. It was mostly worried about you." They're asleep on their feet before you've said thank you. A Pikachu with a flower behind its ear leads them off by the sleeve.

effects.text: Let a child in a straw hat listen to where it hurt.

success.text: They nod, and go back to not fishing.

events.name: The Convertible
events.intro: A red convertible, parked across the whole road. Six cheerleaders. Pom-poms in the rival's colours. Head cheerleader, Trixibelle: "Road's closed! Fan business! Unless you're a fan. Are you a fan?" A cheerleader at the back, quietly: "They're the other one. From the— you know. The other one." Trixibelle: "Oh! Then you'll know three things. Go on. Three things about them. True ones."

success.text: Trixibelle produces a clipboard. Of course she does.
There isn't a round. They chant, for a full minute. It rhymes "best" with "best." Then they move the car anyway.

events.name: The Convertible: One
events.intro: "What did they pick first?"

success.text: Six pom-poms go up at once.
A sharp intake of breath from all six. Trixibelle writes something down.
A sharp intake of breath from all six. Trixibelle writes something down.

events.name: The Convertible: Two
events.intro: "What do they do when they lose?"

success.text: Six pom-poms go up at once.
A sharp intake of breath from all six. Trixibelle writes something down.
A sharp intake of breath from all six. Trixibelle writes something down.

events.name: The Convertible: Three
events.intro: "Who did they stop for?"

choices.label: "Whoever needed it. They'd never say so."

success.text: Six pom-poms go up at once.
A sharp intake of breath from all six. Trixibelle writes something down.
A sharp intake of breath from all six. Trixibelle writes something down.

events.name: The Convertible: The Verdict
events.intro: Trixibelle counts on her fingers. The one at the back is already holding something folded.

success.text: They move the car. The one at the back hands over a folded note: "They talk about you. Don't tell them I said. They'd be unbearable." Where the rival will be next is written underneath.
They chant, for a full minute. It rhymes "best" with "best." Then they move anyway.

events.name: Viridian Night Market
events.intro: The town the region began in. There wasn't a market. There is now: lanterns on strings from the Mart to the Gym, and every stall run by somebody you've met. Where you saw nothing in a town, its stall's kept by a stranger, who says so: "I'm just minding it."

success.text: Pewter's rocks, Cerulean's bait, Vermilion's fish, Celadon's everything. Each one sold by a face you know.
Its keeper, a very small old woman under a very large umbrella: "Things come back, at the end. They get tired of being elsewhere."
You walk the whole length of it once, slowly. Everybody waves.

events.name: Night Market: The Stalls
events.intro: Every price is ten per cent under what it was the first time.

success.text: One of Brock's sisters wraps it in newspaper.
Mr. Holloway pours it into a bottle with great care.
Miss Stott announces her own stall, and then the sale.
Back.

events.name: Viridian Night Market
events.intro: Lanterns on strings from the Mart to the Gym.

success.text: Back to the stalls.
The umbrella, and the small old woman under it.
Everybody waves.

events.name: Night Market: Lost and Found
events.intro: It sells back what you lost to an event in Kanto, at the price it went for.

success.text: It's here. It's still ticking. She won't take money for it: "It was always yours."
A small bottle, wrapped in a gardener's scarf.
"Then nothing's been lost. That happens too."

events.name: Ten Brothers and Sisters

remembers.notice: Nine of them recognise you from the camp. "It's the stew one!"

events.intro: A roadside table. A sign: GENUINE ROCKS. PEWTER SOUVENIRS. A man in a hat pulled low, who looks like somebody. The rock seller, Flint: "You want a rock? No. Nobody does. Listen. I've an errand. One hour. There's ten of them in that house, and my eldest's at work. Mind them. I'll pay in rocks, or in something better."

success.text: Ten faces at the door. Ten opinions about lunch.
He nods, and goes back to not selling rocks.

events.name: The Ten: Cook
events.intro: A pot, six ingredients, ten opinions. Each child says what they hate, once, fast. Pick the three that the most children will eat.

success.text: Eight empty bowls. Two that were licked.
Seven bowls. Three with the onion picked out in a careful pile.
Four bowls. Six polite faces.
Nobody eats it. Everybody says it's fine.

events.name: The Ten: Mend
events.intro: A torn shirt, a broken toy, a scraped knee. Match each to the right fix.

choices.label: Needle, glue, a plaster, and "you're brave."

success.text: The knee wants a plaster and being told it's brave. It gets both.
The knee is fine. It wanted the other thing too.
The shirt is now mostly plaster.

events.name: The Ten: Find
events.intro: Nine children at the table. A count. A recount. The tenth's hiding. Three places to look.

success.text: The tenth, from inside the laundry basket: "I wasn't hiding. I was waiting to be noticed."
Two odd socks, and nobody. She turns up for pudding.
Coats. She turns up for pudding.

choices.label: Let your lead sniff her out.

success.text: Your lead walks straight to the laundry basket and sits beside it. "I wasn't hiding. I was waiting to be noticed."

events.name: The Ten: Home
events.intro: The door. Flint, back from his errand, and someone behind him.

success.text: A home-cooked meal, and a Hard Stone. And Brock, home from work: "You got Suzie out of the basket? She doesn't come out for me." He tells you the road ahead.

effects.text: Minded ten brothers and sisters for an hour, and found the tenth.

success.text: The meal only. It's slightly burnt. The children eat it anyway and tell you it's fine, in the voice people use for that.

events.name: The Water Wheel
events.intro: A shed on the river. A wheel that isn't turning. A cable that goes nowhere. The keeper, a woman eating her lunch on the sluice gate: "Town doesn't need it since the new line. She still works. Put something on the cable if you like. Or put something in the wheel. I pay for the turning; the lights at the school run off it." Shown first: whoever works here starts its next battle at 80% HP. It worked hard.

success.text: It's Charged: Special Attack up on entry for the rest of the stage.

effects.label: Charged at the Water Wheel: Special Attack +1 stage

choices.label: "Turn the wheel." (a Rock or Ground type)

success.text: It turns the wheel. The lights at the school come on. Coins, by its Attack.
It gets wet. It's quite pleased.
She shares it. A small heal.

events.name: The Museum After Hours
events.intro: The museum's side door is open. The guard's asleep in his chair with a sandwich on his chest, going up and down. The fossil hall. Moonlight through the roof. Your own fossil's warm in the bag. Behind the glass of the third case, something turns over.

success.text: An Omanyte, half-woken. Slow, and it hits hard, and it isn't angry. It's confused.
You leave the guard to his sandwich.

events.name: After Hours: The Second Case
events.intro: After the battle it lies down by your bag. It's found the only other thing in the room as old as it is. Then a Kabuto, the same.

success.text: Slow, hard-hitting, bewildered.

events.name: After Hours: The Amber Case
events.intro: The Old Amber's glowing from the inside. The glass has a crack in it that wasn't there this afternoon.

choices.label: "Take it to someone who can wake it properly."

success.text: The Old Amber, to be revived at Cinnabar. A note's left on the guard's sandwich.
Dr. Blackwood, in a dressing gown, within minutes: "Nine years I've sat up with that stone, and it does it the one night I go home." He registers your fossils on the spot.
The glow goes down. In the morning, the crack's gone too.

events.name: After Hours: Shown Out
events.intro: The guard wakes.

success.text: You're shown out, politely, still holding his sandwich by mistake. Nothing's lost.

events.name: Route 3 Rematch Ladder
events.intro: Four trainers standing in a line along the path, a careful ten paces apart, pretending not to know one another. You may stop after any battle; coins for each.

success.text: Youngster Benny: "I like shorts! They're comfy and easy to wear!"
Four people pretend very hard not to watch you go.

events.name: Route 3 Ladder: Lass Janice
events.intro: Youngster Benny, after losing: "They're still comfy. JANICE!"

success.text: Lass Janice: "He always calls me. He always loses first. It's a system."
You keep what you won. The rest of the ladder pretends not to be disappointed.

events.name: Route 3 Ladder: Bug Catcher Robby
events.intro: Lass Janice, after losing: "Robby! Bug boy! You're up!"

success.text: Bug Catcher Robby: "I've got four. They're all the same one. I like that one."
You keep what you won. The rest of the ladder pretends not to be disappointed.

events.name: Route 3 Ladder: Hiker Marcos
events.intro: Bug Catcher Robby, after losing: "MARCOS! ...He'll be a minute. He's big."

success.text: Hiker Marcos: "I let them think it's their ladder."
You keep what you won. The rest of the ladder pretends not to be disappointed.

events.name: The Scientist Who Stayed
events.intro: A thin man in a lab coat at the cave mouth, being mobbed by Zubat, and apologising to them. Seymour: "They're upset about the lamps. Somebody's strung lamps through the whole cave. They can't sleep. I can't sleep. I've written a poem about it. Would you— no. Nobody ever does."

success.text: "'O Clefairy, of the Moon, / You came down in a— a— ' I hadn't a rhyme. I've put 'spoon.' It isn't right."
"Men in black. Very tidy cable work. I've been following it." He shows you where it goes.
"I'll stand behind you and be encouraging." He's no use in a fight, and says so.
He waves at you. The Zubat wave at you. It's hard to tell which is which.

events.name: Seymour: Through the Cave
events.intro: He's walked through Mt. Moon's first two nodes, behind you, being encouraging.

success.text: Nothing stirs. He reads you the poem again, quieter.

failure.text: A Zubat that has had enough of the lamps.

events.name: Seymour: The Moon Stone Chamber
events.intro: He stops in the doorway. The Clefairy are in a ring round the great stone. One of them looks at him, and moves over to make a space. Seymour: "Oh. Oh, I see. I've been writing about it from the outside."

success.text: A Moon Stone, pressed into your hand. He stays. He waves until you're out of sight.

effects.text: Walked a poet to the Moon Stone, and left him in the ring.

events.name: The Serum
events.intro: A side chamber. A portable lamp. A Grunt kneeling by a Rhyhorn, with a case open beside him. Grunt: "Hold still. It's a pinch. They said it's a pinch." The Rhyhorn's too young. It's looking at the case, and it's backed into the wall. What happens next is in the Grunt's face: he flinches, and looks away from it, and it's still happening. A Rhydon's standing where the Rhyhorn was. It's enormous. It's shaking.

choices.label: Stand between it and the wall.

success.text: It attacks the Grunt's lamp, the wall and you, in turn. It isn't choosing. It loses strength every turn.
You back away. Behind you, the Grunt says "easy" over and over, and doesn't mean it.

events.name: The Serum: After
events.intro: The Grunt runs, leaving the case. The Rhydon's on its side, breathing hard.

success.text: Your lead goes to it first. It quietens. It goes off into the dark, slowly, favouring one side.

effects.text: Calmed a Rhydon that had been a Rhyhorn an hour before.

choices.label: "It can't be left like this. Bring it in."

success.text: It comes with you. The game says plainly: it never has to be used in a battle.

events.name: The Serum: Gone
events.intro: The Grunt leaves with it.

success.text: The case is still left behind, empty.

events.name: The Water Ballet
events.intro: A theatre with a glass tank for a stage. A poster: THE MAGICAL MERMAID. Three sisters having one argument in three voices. Daisy: "She's got a cold. You can't have a mermaid who sneezes. The bubbles." Violet: "So we cancel." Lily: "We've sold seats." All three look at your party. Daisy: "...Does that one swim?"

success.text: Your Pokémon is the mermaid's companion.
You're handed water wings. Lily: "The prince doesn't do much. He sinks, attractively."
They cancel. Lily cries a bit. Daisy says she isn't.

events.name: The Water Ballet: Three Movements
events.intro: The Pokémon follows the lead sister through hoops of bubbles. Bond makes the timing kinder.

success.text: Three movements, and the bubbles hold.

failure.text: A hoop missed. The audience claps anyway; they think it's the plan.

events.name: The Water Ballet: The Finale
events.intro: A submarine shaped like a Gyarados comes through the back of the set. Jessie, by loudspeaker: "Prepare for trouble, and make it—" The audience applauds. They think it's the villain. James: "...They like us. Jess. They like us."

success.text: Water moves are stronger in here, and the audience cheers every hit.

events.name: The Water Ballet: Curtain
events.intro: When the submarine's blasted through the roof, it gets a standing ovation, and so does the hole.

success.text: A Mystic Water. And a Seel from the chorus that's taken to your Pokémon asks to come.

effects.text: Saved the Magical Mermaid, and took a bow in water wings.

events.name: The Water Ballet: No Finale
events.intro: The show goes on without a finale.

success.text: The Mystic Water only.

events.name: Pokémon Tech
events.intro: Fog. A gate with a crest. A boy on a treadmill in the yard, holding a candle, being timed by four others. A student with a stopwatch: "He failed the Pidgey question. Level sixteen. Sixteen. Everybody knows eighteen." The boy, Joe: "I beat a Water type with a Grass type on the simulator. It doesn't count, they say. It only counts if it's the answer in the book."

success.text: The stopwatches stop. Joe gets off the treadmill. He looks at you as if nobody has said that before.
A desk, a pencil, and five questions.
"Nothing. That's why it's a punishment."

events.name: Pokémon Tech: Question One
events.intro: Water against Fire?

success.text: A tick.
A cross.

events.name: Pokémon Tech: Question Two
events.intro: Electric against Ground?

success.text: A tick.
A cross.

events.name: Pokémon Tech: Question Three
events.intro: Grass against Flying?

success.text: A tick.
A cross.

events.name: Pokémon Tech: Question Four
events.intro: Ghost against Normal?

success.text: A tick.
A cross.

events.name: Pokémon Tech: The Test
events.intro: Five questions on types and levels. One has an answer that's right in the book and wrong on the road.

success.text: Question one.

events.name: Pokémon Tech: Question Five
events.intro: "At what level does Pidgey evolve?"

success.text: A tick.
It loses the mark, and Joe laughs for the first time.

events.name: Pokémon Tech: The Top Student
events.intro: Giselle: "You've badges. Real ones. I've the equivalent of two, on paper. Shall we find out what paper's worth?" Her Pokémon are level-perfect, with ideal moves. They're badly bonded.

success.text: Giselle, when one hesitates: "That isn't in the— why did it do that?"

events.name: Pokémon Tech: After
events.intro: Giselle: "It looked at me. Mid-match. As if I'd know what to do. ...I've never been looked at like that. I think I'd like to be."

success.text: Wise Glasses. And from Joe, a hand-drawn type chart, with corrections in three colours.

effects.text: Answered the Pidgey question the road's way at Pokémon Tech.

events.name: AJ's Tent
events.intro: A circus tent in a field. A board outside, on a nail: 98 WINS. 0 LOSSES. The 98's on a card that's been changed many times. AJ: "You're ninety-nine. Don't take it personal. At a hundred, I pack the tent and go to the League. I've been promising them that since they were this high." A Sandshrew, a Butterfree, a Rattata, a Beedrill, all with weights tied on.

success.text: His Sandshrew, standing in a tub of water, looking bored. Water moves do it normal damage, not double.
"Took a year. It hated me for six months of it. Ask it now." The Sandshrew splashes him.
"I'm in the tub at five every morning before it is. I don't ask what I don't do."

events.name: AJ's Tent
events.intro: The weights clink. The Sandshrew is still splashing him.

success.text: His Sandshrew, standing in a tub of water, looking bored. Water moves do it normal damage, not double.
He nods. The card stays at 98.

events.name: AJ's Tent: After
events.intro: He looks at the board for a while.

success.text: "...Huh. So that's what it's like. It's not so bad." A Macho Brace.

events.name: AJ's Tent: After
events.intro: He changes the card to 99. "One more. Then they've earned it."

success.text: A Soft Sand, for trying.

events.name: The Bike in the Window

success.text: She's found she likes the road. She keeps going.

events.intro: A shop with one bicycle in the window on a turning stand. The price is on a card: ₽1,000,000. The owner: "It's a very good bicycle."

success.text: "It's a very, very good bicycle."
He takes it without surprise. The Bicycle.
"No. But a great many people have looked. I count that."

events.name: The Bike in the Window
events.intro: It turns on its stand. It is a very good bicycle.

success.text: You count as one of the great many people who have looked.

A smell of burnt rubber. A girl's voice, from a long way off, getting nearer: "HEY!" A girl with a side ponytail and a very carrying voice: "I'm not following you. I'm going the same way. Until I've got a bike."

events.name: The Second Offer
events.intro: The far end of the bridge. The man who stood there's back. No trainers this time. A better coat. The recruiter: "Five in a row. I told head office five in a row, and they said, 'Offer more.' So. More. A salary. A territory. Your friends looked after. You wouldn't have to hurt anybody. You'd just have to not look, on certain days." A card, held between two fingers. It's blank on one side.

success.text: The Inside Man route can be accepted here, early. It's the same offer the evil-team story makes later, and it follows that story's rules; nothing's hidden.
He tips his hat. "Most say no. A few say it like that."
The police are told. Where the Kanto script checks for a police tip, this counts as one.
"If I told you, you'd have to look. That's the whole product."

events.name: The Second Offer
events.intro: The card, still held out.

success.text: He tips his hat. "Most say no. A few say it like that."
The police are told.

events.name: The Girl with the Stall
events.intro: A folding table. A cheerful girl in a wide hat. Rare Candy, Nuggets, a PP Max, a Master Ball, all at a third of the price. The Honest Trade Card's shown, and it's the joke: "Rare Candy (boiled sweet)." "Nugget (painted)." "Master Ball (a Poké Ball with an M drawn on)." The game never lies to you. She does. "Fell off a Silph lorry! Not literally. Legally. Fell off it legally."

success.text: You own a boiled sweet. It's a nice one. It's strawberry.
She comes down, with great suffering, to a quarter. It's still a boiled sweet.
She laughs, properly. "Finally. I've been here all day. Nobody looks." She packs up in six seconds, and leaves one real thing behind for the trouble.
"Your loss! Legally!"

events.name: The River Gyarados
events.intro: The river's the wrong colour and going the wrong way. Something's tearing up the bank. A Gyarados, thrashing. Behind its head, bolted on, a grey collar with a light on it. A fisherman on the bank, hoarse, Mr. Alaric Dunmow: "MARGARET! Margaret, it's me! ...She was a Magikarp eleven years. She evolved the day they took her. She did it to get away." Shown before you accept: she is far stronger than the road.

success.text: The harness is a second target. Three clean hits on it, and the light should go out.
No aiming at the harness. Just her.
Mr. Dunmow doesn't argue. He doesn't look away from the river, either.

events.name: The River Gyarados: The Light Goes Out
events.intro: It cracks. The light goes out. She stops, and looks at the bank.

success.text: Mr. Dunmow: "There you are. There's my girl. Look at the size of you." She's shed a Dragon Scale on the bank.

effects.text: Broke the harness off Margaret the Gyarados, and gave her back to the bank.

success.text: She lays her head on the bank, and he puts both arms round as much of it as he can.

effects.text: Broke the harness off Margaret the Gyarados, and gave her back to the bank.

events.name: The River Gyarados: Stopped
events.intro: She's stopped. The harness is whole.

success.text: Rocket comes for it that night. Mr. Dunmow thanks you anyway, and doesn't look at you.

events.name: The River Gyarados: Downstream
events.intro: She goes downstream.

success.text: She's met again at the Vermilion docks, where the harness can be tried for once more.

events.name: The River Gyarados: The Vermilion Docks
events.intro: The harness light, blinking between the pilings.

success.text: Weaker now, and tired. So are you.
The light goes under the water, and doesn't come up.

events.name: The Capsized Liner
events.intro: You wake on the ceiling. The chandelier's standing up out of the floor. Water at every porthole. James: "Is this the afterlife? It's very like the ballroom." Meowth: "It is the ballroom. We're on the roof of it. The ship's the wrong way up, the sea's the right way up, and there's air for about three rooms." Jessie: "Truce."

success.text: The truce is real for the length of the stage. They don't steal. They don't run. Meowth counts the air: nine turns.
Jessie: "Because I'd rather be arrested than drowned. It's a low bar. I'm clearing it."

events.name: The Capsized Liner: The Stairs
events.intro: The staircase is overhead. One item may be carried from each room.

success.text: It takes one turn of air.

choices.label: A Flying type carries a rope.

success.text: It takes one turn of air.
The trio's Ekans and Weezing make the ladder. One extra turn of air.

events.name: The Capsized Liner: The Fire Door
events.intro: Shut, and warped. One item may be carried from each room.

success.text: It takes one turn of air.

choices.label: Freeze the hinges and break them.

success.text: It takes one turn of air.
Meowth picks it with a claw. One extra turn. "I've had practice. Don't ask where."

events.name: The Capsized Liner: The Hull
events.intro: The way out's through the bottom, which is the top. One item may be carried from each room.

success.text: It takes one turn of air.

choices.label: An Electric move on the rivet line.

success.text: It takes one turn of air.
Koffing and a match. One extra turn, and everybody's eyebrows.

events.name: The Capsized Liner: The Surface
events.intro: Meowth checks the count.

success.text: Daylight. Everybody's on a piece of hull. Nobody says anything for a bit. James: "We should do the motto." Jessie: "We should. In a minute." They don't.

effects.text: Climbed out through the bottom of an upside-down ship with Team Rocket, under a truce.

success.text: Dark. Then: sand. You're washed ashore at 1 HP. One room's item is lost. The trio are further up the beach, alive, arguing about whose fault the sea is.

events.name: Porta Vista

remembers.notice: Moe's is full. He feeds your party free.

events.intro: A beach. A restaurant on stilts with three customers and room for sixty. Next door, a newer one, full, with a loudspeaker. Moe, an old sailor: "Forty years at sea. I bought her to stop moving. Now I owe on her till the end of the week, and I've a boat I was going to sail round the world, and I can't do both." Mrs. Brunhilde Oxley, from her veranda: "He can't do either. I'm not the villain, dear. I'm the arithmetic."

success.text: The party's fed, on a table for sixty with three customers.
Three small jobs: wait on them, call customers in, fix the sign.

choices.label: Enter the Beach Pokémon Talent Contest.

success.text: One of your Pokémon enters. It's judged on Bond, not level.
Moe waves a tea towel.

events.name: Porta Vista
events.intro: The beach, Moe's stilts, and the loudspeaker next door.

success.text: The party's fed, on a table for sixty with three customers.
Three small jobs: wait on them, call customers in, fix the sign.

choices.label: Enter the Beach Pokémon Talent Contest.

success.text: One of your Pokémon enters. It's judged on Bond, not level.
Moe waves a tea towel.

events.name: Porta Vista: Moe's Tables
events.intro: Each job adds to the takings; together they pay a third of the debt.

success.text: A memory game: six orders, nobody writes them down, you get them all to the right table.

failure.text: One soup to the wrong table. They eat it anyway.

success.text: Your most appealing Pokémon stands at the top of the steps. Eleven people come up them.
MOE'S, again, with the S facing the right way.
Back to the beach.

events.name: The Beach Talent Contest
events.intro: Three rounds: an entrance, a talent, a moment with its trainer.

success.text: Judge: "We've seen bigger. We've seen shinier. We haven't seen one look at its trainer like that since— well. Since Moe's old Tentacool." The prize. The debt's paid.

effects.text: Won the Beach Pokémon Talent Contest, and paid off Moe's.

success.text: Not this time. The end of the week. Moe's packing. An envelope under the door: the whole sum, no name. He keeps the place. Mrs. Oxley is seen walking away down the beach without her handbag. "I've no idea what you mean. Arithmetic doesn't have favourites."

events.name: Naptime
events.intro: A harbour street with posters on every pole. Children's faces. All from the last three days. A mother: "He was in the garden. I looked away to hang a sheet." The park. They're all here. They're all fine. One's on all fours in the sandpit, digging. One's on a branch, cooing. One's saying "Psy?" and holding its head. Officer Jenny: "They don't know their names. They're happy as anything. We can't get them home; they keep going back to the grass."

success.text: A door with a brass plate: THE POKÉMON LOVERS' CLUB. MEMBERS ONLY.

events.name: Naptime: The Pokémon Lovers' Club
events.intro: Velvet chairs, tired people in good suits, and a Hypno with its pendulum going. The chairman, Mr. Horatio Favell: "We don't sleep. Any of us. Business. He gives us an hour a night. It's the only hour we have. You'd take it away?"

choices.label: "The waves carry. Come and see the park."

success.text: He comes. He stands at the park railings a long time. "...Mine's eleven. She's at school. She might have been—" He goes back and stops it himself. The Hypno turns its waves round. The children wake, on the grass, puzzled, hungry. The one from the sandpit: "I had a tail. Mum. I had a tail." A Drowzee the club kept as a spare asks to leave with you.

effects.label: A headache lifted: Special Attack doubled

effects.text: Woke the children of the harbour street who thought they were Pokémon.

success.text: The members watch, too tired to object.

choices.label: "Does the Hypno want to be doing this?"

success.text: It doesn't. It's been at it nine nights without rest. It puts the pendulum down the moment somebody asks. The Hypno turns its waves round. The children wake, on the grass, puzzled, hungry. The one from the sandpit: "I had a tail. Mum. I had a tail." A Drowzee the club kept as a spare asks to leave with you.

effects.label: A headache lifted: Special Attack doubled

effects.text: Woke the children of the harbour street who thought they were Pokémon.

events.name: Naptime: After
events.intro: The pendulum on the carpet.

success.text: Mr. Favell doesn't argue. The Hypno turns its waves round. The children wake, on the grass, puzzled, hungry. The one from the sandpit: "I had a tail. Mum. I had a tail." A Drowzee the club kept as a spare asks to leave with you.

effects.label: A headache lifted: Special Attack doubled

effects.text: Woke the children of the harbour street who thought they were Pokémon.

events.name: The Dam

remembers.notice: One Diglett comes up, looks at you, and nods. These Diglett know.

events.intro: A valley. Diggers on their sides. A queue of trainers at a table, and a foreman with a bag of money and no voice left. Foreman Callahan: "Diglett! Every night! Holes under the lorries! A fortune to whoever clears them off. I've had forty trainers. Not one's so much as thrown a Ball. Cowards, the lot." The site. A row of Diglett, watching. You reach for a Poké Ball. It won't open. None of them will. From inside each one: a small, firm no.

success.text: Your party's out of its Balls now, of its own accord, looking up the valley.
The Balls stay shut. Nothing's lost. The foreman pays somebody else, who has the same trouble.
A forest the Diglett planted, and tend, tree by tree.

events.name: The Dam: Up the Valley
events.intro: Dugtrio turning the soil, Diglett carrying seedlings. The dam would put it under forty feet of water. Your party's looking at the trees, and then at you.

success.text: You take the foreman up the valley. He looks. He sits down on a stump. "...Nobody told me there was a forest. It's not on the plan. It's a blank on the plan." The dam's moved. By morning there's a new line of saplings down the road, and a Soft Sand on your bag.
The Balls stay shut. Nothing's lost. The foreman pays somebody else, who has the same trouble.

events.name: The Dam: The Saplings
events.intro: A Diglett is standing by your bag, very still, the way they do when they've decided something.

success.text: It comes.
It goes back down. A sapling, a little straighter than the others.

events.name: The Photographer
events.intro: A bush with a lens in it. A click. Your lead looks round. Another click. Todd, falling out of the bush: "Don't move! No, do. Do what you were doing. I've been hired. A magazine. Two very elegant editors and their cat. They said: 'Capture that one's Pokémon.' So!" He pats the camera. He means: on film. He's no idea they meant anything else.

success.text: He's at the edge of every node from now on. Each thing that happens is a photograph.
"Two editors and a cat. Very elegant. One of them had a rose." He follows along anyway.
He's crushed, and goes. Nothing happens.

events.name: The Photographer: The Album
events.intro: Jessie, earlier, somewhere: "Where is it? The Pokémon?" Todd: "Here! Sixty exposures!" Meowth: "...He took pictures. Of course he did. We said 'capture.' We deserve this." Now he hands the album over, and won't be paid. "I take them of Pokémon. I don't do people. ...There's a few of you in the corners. You kept being where they were looking."

success.text: Coins for one, and a keepsake for the other.

effects.text: Got an album from Todd: sixty exposures, and you in the corners.

success.text: The kindness you didn't think anybody saw.
The trio, blasting off, in focus.

events.name: The Itemfinder
events.intro: A gatehouse with an upstairs. A young man at a desk with a ledger, who's been waiting for anybody at all. The assistant, Mr. Ambrose Tack: "The professor sent me to give this to a trainer who's seen thirty kinds. That was four months ago. May I count yours? I've counted the gulls. There's nine."

success.text: "Thirty-four! Thirty-four. I can go home. I can't remember where it is. I'll find it. I've a device." The Itemfinder: hidden items will beep for the rest of the run.
"Twenty-two. Eight more. I'll be here." He is.
He goes back to the gulls.

events.name: The Itemfinder: Again
events.intro: A Pidgey lands on your shoulder with a note from Mr. Tack: "Count again?"

success.text: "Thirty-four! Thirty-four. I can go home. I can't remember where it is. I'll find it. I've a device." The Itemfinder: hidden items will beep for the rest of the run.
The Pidgey waits, then goes home.

events.name: The Name Rater
events.intro: A front room with a desk, a ledger of every name he's ever rated, and a man who's been rating them out loud to himself. The Name Rater: "Names are my trade. I don't sell them. I assess them. Show me one. I'll tell you what I think, and you won't thank me."

choices.label: Show him one with its species' own name.

success.text: "You've called your Pidgey 'Pidgey.' I call my wife 'Wife.' She's left." He gives it a name of its own. "There. See its ears? It likes having one. They all do. It's the difference between being a thing and being the thing."

choices.label: Show him one with a short name.

success.text: "Serviceable. It'll come when it's called. Most don't."

choices.label: Show him one with a very long name.

success.text: "It's a sentence. You've named it a sentence. By the time you've shouted it, the battle's over."
"Nobody ever thanks me. I've stopped minding. I've not stopped noticing."

events.name: The Listening Post
events.intro: A hill above the town. A shed. An aerial made of fence wire and a coat hanger. The volunteer, Miss Cordelia Wray: "I built it for the music. There's a station from Goldenrod, on a good night. Only there's this, now. Under the music. It isn't music." She turns a dial. A pulse. Short, short, long. A gap. Again. "From the west. Every forty seconds. I've written it down." A notebook: pages of dots. "It never changes. Things that never change, somebody's keeping them that way."

success.text: It's the same pulse. She goes white. "It's talking to them?" She gives you the gap between pulses: that's when a rigged Pokémon is weakest.

effects.label: The gap between pulses: the next rigged Pokémon is easier

choices.label: "Could it be a lighthouse? A buoy?"

success.text: "A lighthouse doesn't stop when you listen." The notebook's a File.
"Since the spring. It got louder the week the Tower had its trouble." The notebook's a File.

events.name: The Channelers' Vigil
events.intro: Three women in white at the Tower's door, with candles. They aren't blinking. The candles are burning sideways. The first: "Give... me... your... all..." Each stands by a stone, and the stone can be read first.

success.text: It works at once.

choices.label: Read the stone, and say the name.

success.text: The stone: "Pippin. Raticate. Eleven years." "Pippin." The candle goes upright. Something small and quick runs out of her, across the grass, and through a headstone as if it's a door. The Channeler: "Oh. He only wanted somebody to say it. They stop saying it, you see. After a while."
Something comes out of her that isn't her.
The candles turn to follow you.

events.name: The Channelers' Vigil: The Second
events.intro: The second: "Zombies!" (She's the only one who seems to be enjoying it.)

success.text: It works at once.

choices.label: Read the stone, and say the name.

success.text: The stone: "Bramble. Growlithe. A good boy." "Bramble." She stops enjoying it, and sits down on the grass, and laughs, and cries a bit.
Something comes out of her that isn't her.

events.name: The Channelers' Vigil: The Third
events.intro: The third says a name. It isn't hers.

success.text: It works at once.

choices.label: Read the stone, and say the name.

success.text: The stone: "Mabel. Clefairy. Sang." "Mabel." Something hums, very quietly, in the key of a lullaby, and stops.
Something comes out of her that isn't her.

events.name: The Channelers' Vigil: The Door
events.intro: Three candles, burning upright.

success.text: They walk you up the Tower's first two floors. Those floors have no wild encounters, and the unseen things stand aside.

effects.text: Said three names at the Tower door, and three candles stood up.

success.text: The door's open. The candles stay lit behind you.

events.name: The Orphan

remembers.notice: Mr. Fuji: "Ah. You've met it already, I think. It came back to wait for you."

events.intro: Under Mr. Fuji's kitchen table, in the furthest corner, something with a skull on its head and its back to the room. A volunteer: "It came from the Tower. It won't eat with the others. Don't try and pull it out. People try. It's worse after."

success.text: You sit. Nothing happens. The clock in the hall. The Psyduck doorstop sighs. The Cubone's turned its head a little.
You leave it be. It doesn't look round. It might have.

events.name: The Orphan: Waiting
events.intro: Longer. A volunteer steps over your legs without comment.

success.text: It's a foot nearer. It's holding its club in both hands.
You leave it be. It doesn't look round. It might have.

events.name: The Orphan: Waiting
events.intro: The light's moved across the floor.

success.text: It's against your knee. It isn't looking at you. It's shaking, and then it isn't. It follows you to the Tower. It isn't a party member, and it doesn't battle.

effects.text: Sat on Mr. Fuji's floor until a Cubone came out from under the table.

success.text: You leave it be. It doesn't look round. It might have.

events.name: The Offering
events.intro: A small building beside the Tower. THE HOUSE OF MEMORIES. A man sweeping a floor that's already clean. The grave-keeper, Mr. Tobias Merriman: "We keep a book. Not only the ones buried here. The ones who didn't get that far, too. The ones who were set down somewhere and left. Is there anybody you'd like to leave something for?" The book is open at this journey's page.

success.text: He wraps it in a cloth, writes the name on a tag, and puts it on a shelf with a great many others. "It'll get there. I couldn't tell you how. I've stopped asking how."

effects.text: Left something at the House of Memories, for one who didn't get this far.

success.text: He wraps it in a cloth, writes the name on a tag, and puts it on a shelf with a great many others. "It'll get there. I couldn't tell you how. I've stopped asking how."

effects.text: Left something at the House of Memories, for one who didn't get this far.

success.text: "One thing, for one. That's the rule. It isn't my rule. If it were for everybody, it'd be for nobody."
He goes back to sweeping. "The book's always open."
